summary: What each released version of the desktop app can do, so an assistant knows which steps it can hand to the app and when to tell the user to update. The app performs every transaction; this MCP server only reads.

local_mcp_bridge.transport: MCP Streamable HTTP, JSON responses, POST http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp (default port 41777), Authorization: Bearer <per-install token>
local_mcp_bridge.enabled_by: Settings, Claude Integration, Turn on (off by default); the same panel shows the token and the claude mcp add command
local_mcp_bridge.confirmation: every spend or signature opens a confirmation in the app window and waits for the user (typed token on MainNet); dry: true previews the command without confirmation
local_mcp_bridge.never_available: owner key import and revoke, application wallet create, recover, import, export: no key or phrase ever crosses the bridge
local_mcp_bridge.servers: named by their Settings entry; SSH key paths never cross the bridge

capabilities: everything in hta-2026-09-14, rebuilt in Electron with the same screens
one-time import of the HTA's settings, wallet records, activity, and keyring passphrase on the same PC
application wallets: create, recover, import, fund, export, remove
delegate an application to a gateway chosen from the live gateway list, and undelegate
settings: services folder, SSH server entries (a server is network-agnostic)
provision one supplier stack per network per server (HA RelayMiner in its own directory, operator key created on the server, one public hostname per network, shared Caddy per server)
deploy a service backend to a provisioned server and connect it to that network's relayer
unstake supplier (signed by the owner wallet; the app shows the live unbonding period and the return block, and an unstaking supplier shows as unstaking until the stake returns)
service lifecycle status per network: created, registered, pending (with the activation block), active
test relays through the protocol with pocket-ap
not_available: no local MCP bridge: the assistant guides the user through the app's buttons rather than driving them

electron-macos.notes: DMG, signing, notarisation; encrypted keyring export/import between machines
